args.title: Query.one_of() must match all documents when given a generator
args.summary: Precise bug report. Currently `Query.one_of(items)` (tinydb/queries.py:476) runs `value in items` once per document. `freeze()` leaves a generator unchanged, so the generator is a one-shot iterator that is consumed by the first documents tested. Later documents then see an exhausted generator and fa…

requirements.statement: When a generator is passed to Query.one_of, the query shall match every document whose tested field value is contained in the values the generator yields, with no document missed because earlier documents were tested.

acceptance_criteria.given: a TinyDB on MemoryStorage holding the documents {'tag':'a'}, {'tag':'b'}, {'tag':'a'}, {'tag':'c'} and allowed = (t for t in ['a','b'])

acceptance_criteria.when: q is called directly with {'tag':'a'}, {'tag':'b'}, {'tag':'a'} and {'tag':'c'} in that order
acceptance_criteria.then: the return values are True, True, True, False

acceptance_criteria.given: a TinyDB on MemoryStorage holding {'tag':'a'}, {'tag':'a'}, {'tag':'b'} and a generator yielding 'a' and 'b'

requirements.statement: When a list is passed to Query.one_of, the query shall keep matching every document whose tested field value is in the list.
requirements.source_quote: With a list it works fine.

acceptance_criteria.when: q is called with {'key1':'value 1'} and then with {'key1':'value 3'}
acceptance_criteria.then: the results are True and False

acceptance_criteria.given: the list ['a','b'] and a query q = Query().tag.one_of(['a','b']) used in two successive db.search calls

requirements.statement: If a single one_of query built from a generator is used in more than one search (Q-001), the system shall return the same matches for each search.

acceptance_criteria.given: documents {'tag':'a'}, {'tag':'c'} and q = Query().tag.one_of(t for t in ['a','b'])
acceptance_criteria.when: db.search(q) is called twice in a row on the same TinyDB

acceptance_criteria.given: q = Query().tag.one_of(t for t in ['a','b']) used on two separate TinyDB instances holding {'tag':'a'}
acceptance_criteria.when: db1.search(q) and then db2.search(q) are called

interpretations: A generator expression or generator-function result, as in the issue example `(t for t in ['a','b'])`. This is the reading the issue actually shows.
Any one-shot iterator (map, filter, file object, iter(...)). The same consumption problem applies, but the issue does not name these.
Any non-list iterable (set, tuple, range, dict view). These can be iterated more than once, so they are a different case from a generator.

terms.term: works fine / matches only some (priority-word mapping)
interpretations: Declarative statements about behaviour ('With a list it works fine', 'expected: ...') map to MUST per the skill's priority rule. No 'should/could' wording is present, so none map to SHOULD or COULD.

open_questions.question: When the same query object built from a generator is used in more than one search, must every search return the same matches (the generator is one-shot, so a second use would otherwise see no values)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The issue only shows one search. Whether repeated use must also work decides FR-QUERY-003, which is a candidate until answered. It does not block FR-QUERY-001.
options: (a) yes, repeated use gives identical results
(b) only a single use is required
(c) repeated use may raise a clear error

open_questions.question: Should other non-list iterables (iterators such as map/filter/iter(), sets, tuples, ranges) also be supported by one_of, or only generators and lists?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The docstring names only 'list or generator'. The scope for other iterables is undetermined.
options: (c) generators, lists and other collections already supported today
open_questions.proposed_default: (a), recorded as ASM-003 (PROVISIONAL); other iterables stay out of scope

open_questions.question: Is the same generator problem expected to be fixed for Query.any and Query.all, which also accept a sequence argument?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The issue is only about one_of. Whether sibling methods are in scope changes the size of the change.
open_questions.proposed_default: (a); any and all are recorded as out of scope

assumptions.text: The requester (the issue author, iDheer) is the decision owner for this change. No maintainer comments are included, so the stakeholder mode is unavailable and every open question stays OPEN.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: A maintainer may decide scope differently, for example by also covering any and all.

assumptions.text: A user who builds a query from a generator expects it to behave consistently if the query object is reused (FR-QUERY-003).
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: If one-time use is acceptable, FR-QUERY-003 should be rejected and withdrawn. If reuse is expected, tests that only check a single search would miss the bug.

assumptions.text: Scope is limited to generators and lists, the two types named in the docstring and the issue.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Other iterators such as map/filter objects would still fail silently after the fix.

out_of_scope: Changing the behaviour of Query.any and Query.all (see Q-003); no change was requested for them.
Supporting arbitrary other iterables or iterators beyond generators and lists, unless Q-002 is answered otherwise.
Changing the type hint, docstring or docs/usage.rst wording for one_of, unless the maintainer asks; the issue treats the docstring as the existing contract.
Design of the fix (for example materialising the generator into a collection when the query is built). This is left to the implementation stage.

Query result caching design. Recorded only as RSK-001: freeze() does not freeze a generator, so the query hash depends on the generator object itself. This was read in tinydb/utils.py:150-169, and the effect is not tested.
